g.title: H1: Today a worker 'claims' a task and the 'task' row carries the run; fleetd splits this into task (planned unit from plan.yaml), attempt (1 run of 1 worker: A1, A2) and lease (the time-limited hold that renews only on earned activity). Readers of today's ledger and code will read 'task' where fleetd means 'attempt' (understand N1).

H2: 'Feature' is also a task kind (kind: feature, a code kind) and a word for any change. In fleetd a Feature is 1 sub-orchestrator, 1 feature branch and 1 pull request holding 1 main idea and its follow-on ideas. Which meaning does each document use (understand N2)?

H3: 'Orchestrator' today is 1 long-lived LLM conversation that receives ideas, creates tasks and reads mail. In fleetd it does not exist: a deterministic idea dispatcher and 1 sub-orchestrator per feature replace it. Today's mail contract still names [orchestrator re #<id>] answers (understand N3).

H4: 'Done' today is a model action (horch ledger done / horch done). In fleetd only the verifier moves a task to done, and 'landed' (on the feature branch) and 'merged' (in the primary branch by content) are later, separate facts. A reader can take 'done' to mean the work reached the primary branch (understand N4).

H5: 'Judgment kind' (research, design, docs, report, creative) and the kind 'judge' sound alike. A judgment task needs a paired judge task; a judge task needs no judge. A resolver task has a code kind. Mixing them breaks plan validation (understand N12).

H6: 'Ready' names 3 states: a task is ready when its dependencies are done (not yet dispatched); a task branch is ready when it is verified and waits for a bundle; a feature is ready when its full gate passed. 'Landed' is both a task branch state and a worktree state. Which one does a status line mean? Answered (design A20): the state names stay, and each status line, event, log line and message that gives a state also gives the kind of its entity. A task is done; its task branch is landed.

H7: The idea row records its feature (ideas.feature_id), but the feature row and branch are written when the sub-orchestrator first writes assumptions. Which feature does an idea with no --to point at between capture and assumptions, and what does horch ideas show for it? Answered (orchestrator, D15): the idea gets its features row at capture and its feature branch at its first assumptions.

H8: The Preservation analysis rows (04 W6, F9, F7, F5, L5, L9, W8, W9, F11, S7, L6, L8, S8, S10, M5, 05 E-10, 06 S1 to S15) are hard inputs. Each must have exactly 1 owner in the model; a row that falls between 2 owners is a behavior fleetd silently drops (understand N15).
H9: What number counts as 'full use' of the subscription usage that pacing aims for? Pacing holds dispatch per pool window, but the design gives no target (understand Q1).

H10: A worker question has 'a time limit' before it escalates, but the design gives no value for it, and it does not say if the limit pauses while the operator is outside working hours. Answered (orchestrator, D15): 15 min with no answer from a running sub-orchestrator, as a starting value. The wait for the operator has no limit.

H11: Plan validation refuses a project that has not declared a fast gate and a full gate, and this repository has no unit-only command today (research-03 F10, understand Q8). Until one is declared, no plan of this repository can commit.

H12: A task gets max_attempts attempts, then 1 replan, then goes to the operator. A requeue resets attempt_floor (04 L8). Does a requeued task also get a new replan, and how does the 2-requeue limit of the review scripts count against attempts? Answered in part (orchestrator, D15): an operator requeue sets the attempt count to 0; a review requeue keeps its own counter. The replan stays open (Q3).

H13: Lease and stall time count only while the machine is awake. If the platform layer reports sleep and wake wrongly on 1 OS, leases expire during a sleep and every worker burns an attempt at wake. Answered (design A25): each timer is a deadline on 1 fleet clock in the ledger, which does not run while the machine sleeps or while fleetd is down. The hang check of fleetd and max_minutes of the wrapper use awake time from the platform layer.

H14: Docs sync and adapter conformance are collapsed to 2 events here. The flow that turns a drift into a task (who owns it, how a profile becomes healthy again) is not stormed. Answered (design, Docs sync and adapter conformance): docs sync is a horch subcommand that fleetd schedules as a docs_sync job, then a conformance job. worker-profiles marks a profile unhealthy and healthy again, and a drift becomes an idea.

H15: A project setting says who merges a feature; the default is the operator. When the setting lets fleetd merge, which gate and which actor stands for the merge decision? Answered (design A28, the feature state table): the owner of a ready feature is the operator, or fleetd when the project sets the merge to automatic. The gate is the full gate on the feature tip over the fetched primary tip.
